page.layout: One column of running text, with the running head above it and the page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: fis mediis certare, Deum ten-tare diceretur, adeoque mira-culosum quem exitum, & eventum sperare. Etsi enim æque Deo possibile, & facile, per paucos, quàm per plures quem liberare, quod accidit cum Jonathan comite armigero Philisteos invasit: quia tamen ad miracula confugien-dum non est, sed ad ordinaria media, facilius erit æquale ab æquali superari, quàm robu-stum ab imbecilliori, aut plu-rimos, à paucissimis. Adeo ut si ratione prudenti omnes cir-cumstantiæ examinentur, tu-tius fit causam belli singulari certamini committere.
Et certè si multis licet ad-versus multos pugnare, quid ni & uni adversus unum; ubi-que enim eadem justitiæ causa, si modò ducis adsit auctoritas & jussus, quem omnino hic desidero.

page.notes: The page number's last digit is printed in the old yogh-like form of 3, so it is given as 9ȝ[?]. The first word "fis" is a fragment of a word cut off at the page's left edge, kept as printed. Small specks and stains around the text (near "exitum", at the right margin and below the text) are not printed text and are left out. The "Præ-" catchword is the only word at the foot of the page.
